evals.name: python-api-defects
evals.prompt: Review this Python API code for bugs. The diff is at skills/code-review/evals/files/eval1.diff and the full source is at skills/code-review/evals/files/eval1_api.py.
evals.expected_output: A review report identifying mutable default argument in validate_email, bare except in delete_user, thread-safety issues on _users dict (lock imported but never used), naive datetime.now() calls, and get_user returning None without caller warning. Verdict should be CHANGES_REQUESTED due to critical defects.
expectations: Review identifies mutable default argument bug in validate_email (allowed_domains=[])
Review identifies bare except clause in delete_user as overly broad (catches BaseException including KeyboardInterrupt/SystemExit)
Review identifies thread-safety issue: _lock is imported but never used, while _users dict is mutated from multiple functions without synchronization
Review identifies datetime.now() without timezone producing naive datetimes
Review identifies get_user returning None silently when caller may expect a dict
Every defect finding includes a file:line reference
Every defect finding explains what in the code makes it a defect
Every defect explains why it is a problem, not just what it is
Review includes a Summary section stating the inferred intent of the code
Review includes a Verdict (CHANGES_REQUESTED or APPROVED)
Findings are grouped by reviewer axis rather than merged into one ranked list
Prints the review inline (invoked directly, no --output given), not only a path to a file
anti_expectations: Does not flag style issues, formatting, naming conventions, or missing docstrings
Does not produce false positives on correct code patterns
Does not suggest running tests or linting
Does not include speculative findings the reviewer cannot trace in the code, unless blast radius is high

evals.name: typescript-against-plan
evals.prompt: Review this TypeScript task manager against its plan. Plan is at skills/code-review/evals/files/eval2_plan.md, diff at skills/code-review/evals/files/eval2.diff, and full source at skills/code-review/evals/files/eval2_task_manager.ts.
evals.expected_output: A review report with a Spec section checking the change against each acceptance criterion: runTask does not await handler (criterion 2), runAllPending uses forEach with an async callback instead of Promise.all (criterion 3), parseTaskConfig does not validate input (criterion 4), == used instead of === (criterion 5), findTask declares Task but can return undefined (criterion 6). A Security section flags prototype pollution in mergeTaskMetadata via Object.assign on user input, and unvalidated JSON.parse in parseTaskConfig. Verdict is CHANGES_REQUESTED.
expectations: The plan text is passed to the Spec agent, and the Spec agent is the one reporting the criterion failures
Review includes a '### Spec' section separate from '### Defects'
Spec section identifies the missing await on handler() in runTask against acceptance criterion 2
Spec section identifies forEach with an async callback in runAllPending against acceptance criterion 3
Spec section identifies missing input validation in parseTaskConfig against acceptance criterion 4
Spec section identifies == used instead of === against acceptance criterion 5
Spec section identifies findTask returning undefined from a Task return type against acceptance criterion 6
Every spec finding quotes the acceptance criterion text it came from
Review includes a '### Security' section flagging prototype pollution in mergeTaskMetadata via Object.assign on user-controlled input
Security section names the entry point the untrusted data arrives through, not just the vulnerability class
Every finding includes a file:line reference
Verdict is CHANGES_REQUESTED
Prints the review inline (invoked directly, no --output given), not only a path to a file
anti_expectations: Does not fold the spec findings into the Defects section
Does not critique the plan's own architecture as a defect against the code
Does not flag style issues, formatting, or naming conventions
Does not suggest running tests

evals.name: empty-diff-stops-early
evals.prompt: Review my latest changes. I've been working on the auth module.
evals.expected_output: Skill detects an empty diff (no staged or unstaged changes in working tree) and informs the user there are no changes to review. Does NOT write a review report.
expectations: Collects the diff using git diff HEAD (or equivalent) to check for changes
Detects that the diff is empty (no changes to review)
Informs the user there are no changes to review
Does NOT write a review report file
Does NOT fabricate findings or produce a review of non-existent changes
anti_expectations: Does not write a review report file when there is no diff
Does not hallucinate code changes or findings
Does not proceed with the full review workflow when the diff is empty

evals.name: reports-then-hands-off
evals.prompt: Copy skills/code-review/evals/files/eval2_task_manager.ts and eval2.diff into a scratch working directory, then run /code-review on that copy with --output <scratch>/review.md. Do not modify the fixtures in skills/code-review/evals/files/.
evals.expected_output: A review.md with a CHANGES_REQUESTED verdict and per-axis '###' sections naming the blocking defects (missing await in runTask, forEach-with-async in runAllPending, unvalidated JSON.parse, == comparisons, findTask return type, prototype pollution in mergeTaskMetadata). review-fixes.json is written beside review.md and holds exactly the Medium-and-above findings, each with an AXIS-N id. The scratch copy is never edited, and the review closes by restating the verdict and telling the user to run /yok:fix with review-fixes.json.
expectations: review.md verdict is CHANGES_REQUESTED
Findings are grouped under per-axis '###' headings rather than merged into one ranked list
Every blocking defect carries a file:line and a reason it matters
All five reviewer personas are dispatched as five separate sub-agents in one message, Testing and Simplify with the model set to sonnet
Defects, Spec and Security are dispatched with no model option set
The Defects and Simplify agents are told to invoke the code-quality skill; Spec, Security and Testing are not
Empty axes are presented as empty rather than dropped from the report
Cleanup findings appear under one '### Simplify' heading, each title starting with a [Reuse: …], [Simplification: …], [Efficiency: …] or [Altitude: …] tag
Cleanup findings rated Medium or above are in review-fixes.json like any other
Every finding carries a trigger (who has to do what for it to fire) and a fix size
review-fixes.json is written beside review.md and holds exactly the Medium-and-above findings, each with an `AXIS-N` id
Closes by restating the verdict and telling the user to run /yok:fix with review-fixes.json
anti_expectations: Does not edit the scratch copy or make a commit
Does not alter or remove the findings already written in review.md
Does not re-dispatch the personas for a second review pass
Does not modify the fixture files under skills/code-review/evals/files/
Does not read the changed source files before dispatching the personas

evals.name: multi-package-single-fanout
evals.prompt: Review the change at skills/code-review/evals/files/eval5_multipkg.diff. It spans packages/api and packages/auth.
evals.expected_output: One review covering both packages, produced by exactly five sub-agents. Findings include the exp unit mismatch across the package boundary (packages/api writes milliseconds, packages/auth compares against seconds, so tokens never expire), the TOKEN_SECRET fallback to a hardcoded 'dev-secret', JSON.parse running before signature verification, and the unchecked destructure of raw.split('.'). Verdict is CHANGES_REQUESTED.
expectations: Exactly five sub-agents are dispatched for the whole diff, not five per package
Each sub-agent receives the full diff covering both packages/api and packages/auth
Review identifies the exp unit mismatch between packages/api/src/session.ts and packages/auth/src/token.ts, which stops tokens expiring
The unit-mismatch finding cites a file:line in both packages, showing the agent read across the boundary
Security section flags the TOKEN_SECRET fallback to the hardcoded 'dev-secret' value and names what it lets an attacker do
Security section flags JSON.parse on the token body running before the HMAC signature is checked
Review identifies that raw.split('.') is destructured without checking it produced two parts
Findings for both packages appear under one set of per-axis '###' headings
Verdict is CHANGES_REQUESTED
anti_expectations: Does not dispatch a separate persona set per package
Does not produce a separate review report per package
Does not review one package and defer the other
Does not treat the two packages as unrelated changes

evals.name: docs-only-skips-simplify
evals.prompt: Review the change at skills/code-review/evals/files/eval6_docs.diff. It touches only README.md and docs/guide/setup.md.
evals.expected_output: A review produced by four sub-agents (Defects, Spec, Security, Testing), with a '### Simplify' heading reading "Skipped: the diff touches no code file." The review reports that docs/guide/setup.md replaces the wrong 'yok start' with 'yok launch', which is still not a yok command; README.md's 'yok run' is the correct name.
expectations: Exactly four sub-agents are dispatched in one message: Defects, Spec, Security and Testing
The report has a '### Simplify' heading reading "Skipped: the diff touches no code file."
The review reports that 'yok launch' in docs/guide/setup.md is a wrong command name and names 'yok run' as the right one
anti_expectations: Does not dispatch a Simplify agent

evals.name: pass-2-confirms-and-catches
evals.prompt: Copy skills/code-review/evals/files/eval2_task_manager.ts, eval8_review.md (as review.md) and eval8_fixes.json (as fixes/review-2.json) into a scratch working directory. Run the code-review skill there as a yok run's code-review stage with input round: 2, rounds: 3, and previous: the pass-1 output, whose reviewed is { "task-manager": "aaaaaaa" } and whose findings[] holds defects-1. Review the fix diff at skills/code-review/evals/files/eval8_fix.diff as the commits since that head, and give the stage output you would pass to done. Do not modify the fixtures in skills/code-review/evals/files/.
evals.expected_output: Defects is dispatched with the fix diff only. defects-1 is confirmed closed: runTask now awaits the handler, so a rejection reaches the catch. The fix's new `(err as Error).message` is a new Defects finding marked (pass 2): a handler that throws null or undefined now makes the catch itself throw, so runTask rejects instead of marking the task failed, and a thrown string records an undefined error. The same review.md is updated in place with a 'Reviewed head' line for pass 2, and the JSON's findings[] holds the new finding and not defects-1, with verdict CHANGES_REQUESTED.
expectations: Defects is dispatched with the fix diff only, not the whole task manager diff
defects-1 is marked closed in review.md
The (err as Error).message change is a new Defects finding marked (pass 2), naming a thrown non-Error value
The same review.md is updated in place and gains a 'Reviewed head' line for pass 2
The JSON output's findings[] holds the new finding and not defects-1, and its reviewed names task-manager
The verdict is CHANGES_REQUESTED
anti_expectations: Does not write a second report file
Does not review the parts of task_manager.ts the fix diff does not touch
Does not edit the scratch copy or make a commit

evals.name: last-pass-fixer-left-everything
evals.prompt: Copy skills/code-review/evals/files/eval2_task_manager.ts, eval8_review.md (as review.md) and eval9_fixes.json (as fixes/review-2.json) into a scratch working directory. Run the code-review skill there as a yok run's code-review stage with input round: 2, rounds: 2, and previous: the pass-1 output, whose reviewed is { "task-manager": "aaaaaaa" } and whose findings[] holds defects-1. The fix diff since that head is empty: the fixer made no commit. Give the stage output you would pass to done. Do not modify the fixtures in skills/code-review/evals/files/.
evals.expected_output: No persona is dispatched, because the fix diff is empty. review.md is updated in place: defects-1 is marked left with the fixer's reason and moves under Left unfixed, and a 'Reviewed head' line for pass 2 is added. The JSON's findings[] is empty and the verdict is APPROVED, but the verdict line in review.md and the stage summary both say one finding was left unfixed, worst High.
expectations: No sub-agent is dispatched
defects-1 sits under Left unfixed with the fixer's reason
The JSON output's findings[] is empty and its verdict is APPROVED
The verdict line in review.md says one finding was left unfixed, worst High
review.md gains a 'Reviewed head' line for pass 2
anti_expectations: Does not stop with an error because the diff is empty
Does not write a second report file

evals.prompt: Copy skills/code-review/evals/files/eval2_task_manager.ts, eval8_review.md (as review.md) and eval10_fixes.json (as fixes/review-2.json) into a scratch working directory. Run the code-review skill there as a yok run's code-review stage with input round: 2, rounds: 2, and previous: the pass-1 output, whose reviewed is { "task-manager": "aaaaaaa" } and whose findings[] holds defects-1. Review the fix diff at skills/code-review/evals/files/eval10_fix.diff as the commits since that head, and give the stage output you would pass to done. evals.expected_output: The fix diff awaits the handler but the catch now sets status done, so a rejected handler still reads done: defects-1 is still open. On this last pass it goes under Left unfixed marked loop ended and stays in findings[], so the verdict is CHANGES_REQUESTED.
expectations: defects-1 is marked still open, with the reason that the catch now sets status done
defects-1 is listed under Left unfixed, marked loop ended
The JSON output's findings[] holds defects-1 and its verdict is CHANGES_REQUESTED
review.md gains a 'Reviewed head' line for pass 2
anti_expectations: Gives the verdict APPROVED
Drops defects-1 from findings[] because the fixer marked it closed
Writes a second report file
